rule: Daily fat floor 72 g (~0.8 g/kg at ~90 kg; ~23% of 2834 kcal), kept before carbs are allocated
summary: A meta-analysis of 6 intervention studies (206 men) found low-fat diets lowered total and free testosterone compared with high-fat diets (SMD about -0.38). That argues for a floor, not for any particular number. Consensus ranges are 0.5-1.5 g/kg (off-season review), 15-30% of energy (contest prep) and ~30% (with 0.5-1 g/kg acceptable when cutting) per the ISSN. 72 g (~0.8 g/kg, ~23% at maintenance, ~28% in a cut) sits inside all of them while leaving room for hard-day carbs. The evidence supports keeping a floor in this range; the exact number is still a judgement.

sources.note: Low-fat vs high-fat diets in men: total T SMD -0.38, free T -0.37; stronger in European/N American men; small, low-certainty evidence
ISSN 2018: ~30% of kcal from fat generally; 0.5-1 g/kg/day (as little as ~20% kcal) when reducing body fat; higher-fat diets maintain testosterone better
Contest prep: 15-30% of calories from fat
